messages.author: a28ce37a2d809bbf
messages.subject: Extracting area from UD object
parts:
Hi Chris,

Is it possible to directly extract the home range area estimates (CI) from a UD object? I have looked through all of the list elements in the UD object and I can't find them there. When I looked through the github code, it looks like they are calculated in the summary() call. Am I missing something obvious? I have hundreds of UDs and am trying to calculate the average home range size, so it would be great if there was a way to extract them in a loop and calculate the average from that. Right now, I am limited to copying and pasting them from individual summary outputs.

I appreciate any insight you could give me!

Many thanks in advance,
Jenny

messages.author: a28ce37a2d809bbf
messages.subject: Re: Extracting area from UD object
parts:
Answered my own question! For those curious, you can assign the summary(UD) to an object and extract the values from there.

e.g.:

udSummary <- summary(UD)
low <- udSummary$CI[1]
est <- udSummary$CI[2]
high <- udSummary$CI[3]

Cheers,
Jenny

For eg:

area (square kilometers) 1.891947 2.149911 2.424121

and ind1_UD

Regards,

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Extracting area from UD object
parts:
Hi Ushma,

If you plot the two objects, you can see that they look different (Gaussian versus KDE) and should have different areas. The Gaussian estimate assumes a particular model, but has better statistical efficiency. If the data are not Gaussian, then the Gaussian estimate is just estimating variance, which is still meaningful, but is not exactly area.

If you have larger effective sample sizes and are interested in areas, then you want AKDE. If you have smaller effective sample sizes and are willing to suffice with a proxy for area, then you might consider the Gaussian estimates.

Best,
Chris
